rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes adding ~0.5 at% Hf to a dual-phase refractory HEA, while the target paper added 4.2 at% Cr to a single-phase BCC HfMoTaTiZr alloy. These are different elements, different base alloys, and different addition amounts, representing a different specific lever.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis specifies tensile testing at ~1073 K and room temperature, whereas the target paper performed room-temperature compression testing. The temperature regimes and loading modes are different, so the conditions do not match the paper's regime.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes Hf-rich precipitates hindering grain-boundary sliding and dislocation motion at high temperatures. The target paper's mechanism involves solid solution hardening from Cr and crack propagation hindrance from a reticulated Laves phase. These are different general classes of mechanism (precipitation strengthening vs. solid solution + second-phase morphology effect).
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts improved high-temperature strength and ductility, while the target paper reports improved room-temperature yield strength and fracture strain. The property direction (improvement) is the same, but the temperature regime and specific property values differ, so it is only a general agreement on improvement.
